clue.text: Maybe Nubian eunuch was a scoundrel

parts.note: a Nubian, from the Upper Nile, is a black African
eunuchs served as guards of the harem

explanation.surface: A palace harem's eunuch turns out to have been a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nubian eunuch suggests a harem guard of black African origin, which spelt as one word is a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a rogue or villain, an old-fashioned term of abuse for a dishonourable man.

clue.text: Break open the chest

definitions.meaning: to burst or smash something open
a woman's bosom, or a sculpture of head and shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: Burst or smash is one sense; the bosom or upper torso is the other.

clue.text: Building materials for a castle in Spain?

definitions.text: Building materials for a castle in Spain?

parts.words: Building materials for a castle in Spain?
parts.note: a castle in Spain is a daydream, also called a castle in the air, so its bricks would be bricks of the air

explanation.surface: A builder asks what to order for a Spanish fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'castle in Spain' is an idiom for an impossible dream, the same as a castle in the air; the answer is really perforated bricks for ventilation.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforated bricks let ventilation through walls, a real building material punningly suited to a fantasy castle in the sky.

clue.text: Wells' novel laboratory apparatus

definitions.meaning: an H. G. Wells novel of 1905 about a draper's assistant who inherits money
the apparatus named after the Dutch chemist Petrus Kipp, for producing gases

explanation.definitionFit: The title of an H. G. Wells book, and the chemist's gas generator named after its inventor.

clue.text: About 1000 freed from their bonds, and not watched

indicators.note: the word for released goes about, around, the Roman numeral

parts.note: freed from their bonds means untied, with ropes undone
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Prisoners released in their hundreds go unobserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts UNTIED round M. 'Watched' here means checked against a watch, a stopwatch timing.
explanation.definitionFit: A race or event with no clock kept on it has not been measured with a stopwatch.

clue.text: Plump for a civic building

parts.note: plump means rotund, round and fat

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a town hall, 'plump for' meaning opt for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump for' reads as 'choose', but plump is the adjective for fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A round, often domed, building or hall, typical of grand public architecture.

clue.text: Beheaded, its sting would prove more venomous

definitions.text: Beheaded, its sting would prove more venomous

parts.words: Beheaded, its sting would prove more venomous
parts.note: the stinging insect without its first letter becomes a poisonous snake, whose bite is deadlier

explanation.surface: A grim observation that cutting the head off a creature only makes its sting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the head letter off and the insect becomes ASP, Cleopatra's venomous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped stinging insect whose name minus its first letter is a deadly snake.

clue.text: Does it hurt when trodden on in the oak forest?

definitions.text: Does it hurt when trodden on in the oak forest?

parts.words: Does it hurt when trodden on in the oak forest?
parts.note: read as two words, the first a single article and the second a hard patch on a toe that hurts underfoot; whole, it is the oak's seed on the forest floor

explanation.surface: A walker wonders whether stepping on things in an oak wood is painful.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into an article plus the painful patch of hard skin on a toe that hurts when someone treads on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak, which litters the forest floor and is underfoot there.

clue.text: Allocate perfect area of Shetland for official French residence

indicators.note: to allocate is to share out or distribute, so the letters are dealt out in a new order

parts.note: Ure is a small settlement in Northmavine on Shetland's mainland

explanation.surface: Someone is told to assign an ideal patch of the Shetland Isles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allocate' rearranges PERFECT into PREFECT; URE is a small place on Shetland, the Scottish island group.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a prefect, the state's representative in a department, works and lives in this office.

clue.text: Heavenly food supplied by Frenchman with brother in Asia

indicators.note: the Frenchman and his brother are placed in the name of the continent

parts.note: taken as written
M is short for Monsieur, a French gentleman

explanation.surface: Celestial fare served by a Frenchman whose brother lives in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal; M for Monsieur is a standard crossword abbreviation, and 'supplied by' is mere link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the food of the gods, conferring immortality.

clue.text: Take off area for taking off

definitions.meaning: a runway or airstrip where aircraft take off

explanation.definitionFit: To undress is one sense; a landing runway is the other.

clue.text: Brave standard to speed the French

parts.note: taken as written
tempo means speed, the pace of music
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An instruction to quicken a standard, perhaps a flag, in French.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brave' is a Native American warrior, and his tribe's carved emblem is the 'standard'.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved pole bearing tribal emblems, set up as a sign of a Native American people.

clue.text: One whose studies have not yet fagged him

definitions.text: One whose studies have not yet fagged him

parts.words: One whose studies have not yet fagged him
parts.note: fagged means tired, so the student is still fresh, a newcomer to college

explanation.surface: A student who has not yet been worn out by work.
explanation.walkthrough: Fagged is British slang for exhausted; it also recalls fagging, older boys' use of juniors in public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-year undergraduate, so new to study that it has not tired him.

clue.text: Extent to which anger has developed

indicators.note: developed means the letters of the word have grown into a new form

explanation.surface: Asking how far someone's temper has escalated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' rearranges ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope or reach, how far something goes.

clue.text: Moon starer by disposition

indicators.note: disposition is arrangement, so the letters of the two words are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone temperamentally inclined to gaze at the Moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By disposition' rearranges MOON STARER; the whole clue also describes the scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies the heavens professionally gazes at Moon and stars by nature.

clue.text: A bank loan has usually got to be obtained

definitions.text: A bank loan has usually got to be
definitions.meaning: banks normally require a loan to be backed by collateral

explanation.surface: A remark about bank lending practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan backed by collateral is one sense; achieved or acquired is the other.

clue.text: Give back seat to the Right Excellent the papal ambassador

parts.note: E is the grade for excellent
a legate is the Pope's envoy

explanation.surface: A prelate with honorific titles is demoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right Excellent' reads like a title of honour, but each word gives just its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote is to put someone into a lower position, as a team sent down a division.

clue.text: Attack a fool repulsed last month

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the word for fool is read backwards

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ult., ultimo, means of last month in old letter writing

explanation.surface: An assault on someone, then a fool beaten back in the previous month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repulsed' turns ASS into SSA. ULT is short for ultimo, an old business-letter term for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a violent onslaught.

clue.text: Went fishing after crazy nut got the fishing line sorted out

indicators.note: after puts the fishing word behind the jumbled letters
crazy says the three letters go wild and come out in another order

parts.note: angled means went fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: After an eccentric goes fishing, he sorts out his tangled line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' scrambles the three letters and 'after' sets the fishing verb behind them; 'got the fishing line' just extends the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Freed from knots, straightened out.

clue.text: Stock taker who gets a move on

definitions.meaning: a thief of livestock, a cattle thief
to rustle is to hurry, in American slang

explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief takes stock literally, and one who hustles moves fast.

clue.text: Does it result in a mixed marriage?

definitions.text: Does it result in a mixed marriage?

parts.words: Does it result in a mixed marriage?
parts.note: love affairs lead to marriage, and split as Roman plus CE it is a Roman Catholic wedding a Church of England partner

explanation.surface: A question about whether love leads to an inter-faith wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England; ROMAN suggests Roman Catholic, so the parts make a mixed marriage of faiths.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair, which may lead to a wedding.

clue.text: Agricultural tower

parts.note: read tower as one who tows, a farm vehicle that pulls ploughs

explanation.surface: A tall structure on a farm, perhaps a silo.
explanation.walkthrough: Tower is not a tall building but someone or something that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm vehicle used to pull ploughs and trailers.

clue.text: Its tree planted streets charm the Adriatic tourist

indicators.note: planted suggests set in the ground in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tree-lined avenues delight holidaymakers on the Adriatic coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planted' rearranges ITS and TREE. The definition reads with 'Its' as a city whose streets charm visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian port city on the Adriatic, known for elegant avenues that attract visitors.

clue.text: Clever chap, but he'll have to drink his beer from the bottle!

definitions.meaning: someone who is not a fool or dupe

definitions.text: he'll have to drink his beer from the bottle!
definitions.meaning: a man without a beer tankard has to swig from the bottle

explanation.definitionFit: Someone shrewd is not a fool, and a drinker lacking a tankard must swig straight from the bottle.

clue.text: Toast of the operatic world of the twenties

definitions.text: Toast of the operatic world of the twenties

parts.words: Toast of the operatic world of the twenties
parts.note: the celebrated Australian soprano Dame Nellie, idolised in that era, also gave her name to thin crisp toast

explanation.surface: A famous singer celebrated in 1920s opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' means both a celebrated person and the crisp bread named after the soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Nellie of that name was an acclaimed soprano, and thin dry toast is named after her.

clue.text: It may be visible from an island, but mother isn't near the coast

definitions.text: It may be visible from an island

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
inland means away from the sea

explanation.surface: A distant shore can be seen from an island, though mother lives far from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the larger landmass of a country, seen across the water from an offshore island.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal landmass of a country, as opposed to its offshore islands.

clue.text: Articulate Scandinavians become invalid

indicators.note: articulate means spoken clearly, so the word for these northern people is said out loud

parts.note: Lapps are the people of northern Scandinavia, now usually called Sami

explanation.surface: Well-spoken Nordic people fall into poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective praising the Scandinavians but signals a homophone; 'invalid' means void, not sickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy or claim that expires or lapses becomes void.

clue.text: A great bell split by Rutherford

parts.note: Great Tom is the large bell of Christ Church, Oxford

explanation.surface: A large bell cracked by someone called Rutherford.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Tom is the big bell in Tom Tower at Christ Church, Oxford. Ernest Rutherford's team first split the nucleus in 1932.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist Ernest Rutherford's laboratory first broke apart this basic particle of matter.

clue.text: Limit set by workers Kinnock regards as a problem

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters of limit are put into a different order

parts.note: worker ants are the classic workers

explanation.surface: A cap fixed by trade unionists that the Labour leader finds troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' rearranges LIMIT. Neil Kinnock, Labour leader in the 1980s, fought the Militant Tendency within his party.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Militant Tendency, a hard-left faction Kinnock expelled from Labour.

clue.text: Devout group needs someone at the helm

parts.note: pi is slang for pious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A religious community needs a leader to steer it.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is short for pious, a British schoolboy word for sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steers a ship, or guides it into harbour.

clue.text: Genuine eighth of a piece of eight

definitions.text: eighth of a piece of eight
definitions.meaning: the old Spanish silver dollar, the piece of eight, was worth eight of these coins

explanation.definitionFit: Authentic is one sense; a Spanish silver coin worth an eighth of a dollar is the other.

clue.text: Distribution of free rum about to finish by popular vote

indicators.note: about places the jumbled drink letters around the word for finish
distribution of means the letters are shared out again in another order

parts.note: end means to finish

explanation.surface: Handing out free rum at the close of a public vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribution of' rearranges FREE RUM into REFERUM; 'about' puts it round END.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct vote by the whole electorate on a single question.
